spUNpyF58BY.summary: 3Blue1Brown's animated visual introduction to the Fourier Transform, showing how a signal breaks into frequency components.
spUNpyF58BY.why: HN's default recommendation for understanding the Fourier transform intuitively; many say it was the explanation that made it click.

s1i-dnAH9Y4.summary: A 1953 US Navy training film explaining the basic mechanisms in mechanical fire control computers aboard ships. It shows how gears, differentials and cams solved mathematical problems in permanent mechanical form.
s1i-dnAH9Y4.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as a beautiful, approachable explanation of analog mechanical computation, and many have rewatched it.

sWblpsLZ-O8.summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Linus Akesson that fits video and music into 256 bytes, winning the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2017. A technical write-up accompanies it.
sWblpsLZ-O8.why: It is HN's favorite example of extreme code compression, a compelling song and visuals from a program smaller than a tweet.

s7tWHJfhiyo.summary: CGP Grey explains first-past-the-post voting and why it pushes elections toward two dominant parties. It is the first in his series on electoral systems.
s7tWHJfhiyo.why: HN's go-to explainer for why FPTP leads to a two-party system, linked in countless voting-reform and US politics threads.

snAhsXyO3Ck.summary: CGP Grey argues that your brain treats a whole home as one room during lockdown, blurring work, rest and leisure. He recommends creating separate spaces and routines for different activities to stay balanced.
snAhsXyO3Ck.why: HN recommends it constantly in work-from-home, burnout and procrastination threads as practical advice for separating work from life at home.

stxVBJem3Rs.summary: Jeff Vogel of Spiderweb Software gives a GDC 2018 retrospective on surviving as an indie game maker since 1994, from shareware days through Steam. It covers business realities, costs and sustaining a comfortable living without chasing riches.
stxVBJem3Rs.why: HN keeps recommending it as an inspirational, funny talk on running a long-lived indie studio and what Steam provides for its 30% cut.

sGG-A80Tl5g.summary: Joseph Everett, with Dr. Frank Mitloehner, argues that eating less meat will not do much for the climate. He covers beef's water footprint, land and feed use, and methane.
sGG-A80Tl5g.why: HN commenters recommend it as a counterpoint to claims about beef's environmental cost, though some critique its methane argument.

s86-Z-CbaHA.summary: Vsauce's roughly 24 minute explainer on the Banach-Tarski paradox, building from infinity and set theory to the decomposition of a sphere into pieces that form two spheres.
s86-Z-CbaHA.why: Recommended as an accurate, entertaining on-ramp to set theory and infinity, worth pausing and rewatching.

sPhpelUfu8Q.summary: Juan Pedro Bolivar Puente explains immutable and persistent data structures in C++ and how they support value semantics. He presents the Immer library, rrb-trees, and a prototype text editor that opens a huge file instantly.
sPhpelUfu8Q.why: HN people point to it for rrb-trees, text editor data structures and bringing Clojure-style persistent structures to C++.

sG9UMMq2dz4.summary: Austin Meyer, developer of the X-Plane flight simulator, explains how he was sued by a patent troll over a trivial claim about an app's license server. He walks through how the shell-company litigation works and why ignoring the suit makes things worse.
sG9UMMq2dz4.why: HN commenters pass it around as an eye-opening first-hand account of patent trolling and the Texas courts that favor it.

s_fkpZSnz2I.summary: Irving Finkel of the British Museum tells how a 4,000-year-old cuneiform tablet came to him for examination. It revealed the oldest known account of Noah's Ark and led to a book and a documentary.
s_fkpZSnz2I.why: HN recommends it as a funny, fascinating talk on cuneiform tablets and the ancient world by an engaging curator.

sD0NjbwqlYw.summary: 3Blue1Brown visualizes the Riemann zeta function and the analytic continuation that extends it beyond where its series converges, building toward the Riemann hypothesis.
sD0NjbwqlYw.why: HN praises its visualizations, its handling of the -1/12 result, and its ending, and often prefers it to other explanations of the topic.

sULa9Lc4pck.summary: 3Blue1Brown presents the Triangle of Power, an alternate notation that unifies powers, logarithms and roots in a single triangular symbol. The video shows how the inverse operations relate and how the notation could help.
sULa9Lc4pck.why: HN points to it in notation debates as a clean visual demonstration that exponents, logs and roots are three views of one relationship.

sj8Sg8qnjOg.summary: Numberphile's Ben Sparks shows why the golden ratio is the most irrational number, using seeds, continued fractions and rational approximations. He also explains why plants use it for spacing leaves and seeds.
sj8Sg8qnjOg.why: HN calls it illuminating for explaining why phi is the most irrational number, relevant to hashing, spirals and phyllotaxis.

sqEyWLGvvdw.summary: The first lecture of Francis Su's Harvey Mudd real analysis course, covering the construction of the rational numbers. It begins a full lecture series that follows a standard analysis text.
sqEyWLGvvdw.why: HN people recommend Su's lectures for building real analysis intuition, citing his phenomenal teaching style.

sw0VfmXKq54.summary: In an Ars Technica War Stories episode, Prince of Persia creator Jordan Mechner describes how he made the game on the Apple II, fighting hardware memory limits and the platform's decline. It covers the rotoscoped animation and the engineering tricks involved.
sw0VfmXKq54.why: Repeatedly called essential viewing for game development history and clever work under memory constraints.

skos4B5x7qE.summary: Without Boats, a Rust language team member, explains the design of Rust's async/await at RustLatam 2019. He covers the history and constraints behind zero-cost, allocation-free async state machines.
skos4B5x7qE.why: Recommended during the await syntax debates for explaining the constraints that shaped Rust's async design.

slDAvewWfrA.summary: A clip from the BBC series Britain from Above showing UK peak power demand. It shows a grid engineer preparing for the surge as millions put the kettle on when a popular show ends.
slDAvewWfrA.why: HN cites it as the canonical illustration of TV pickup and grid balancing, and as a must-see example of demand spikes.

smStEPSRKBs.summary: Retro Game Mechanics Explained dissects how Atari's Quadrascan vector displays and vector generator hardware drew games like Asteroids and Tempest.
smStEPSRKBs.why: Recommended whenever Atari vector games come up as an excellent, deep technical explanation of how they worked.

sK5i-N34im8.summary: Jérôme Petazzoni explains how Linux containers are built from kernel features like cgroups, namespaces and SELinux. He demonstrates putting the pieces together by hand to make a container and compares runtimes and approaches like jails and zones.
sK5i-N34im8.why: HN recommends it as a talk that makes containers click, showing that containerization is not virtualization and demystifying what Docker does.

sTJ7AzBIJoI.summary: The original music video for Everybody's Free to Wear Sunscreen, a spoken-word piece built on Mary Schmich's 1997 column of life advice, produced by Baz Luhrmann.
sTJ7AzBIJoI.why: Posted as timeless, comforting life advice in threads about careers, aging, and uncertainty.

sWgDk-o-6ZE.summary: Sean Parent's CppCon 2015 talk on better use of standard containers and the goal of having no incidental data structures. It argues that proper containers can greatly simplify code.
sWgDk-o-6ZE.why: Commenters say it changes how you think about types and the STL, and makes a case for simple modern C++.

s_osQvkeNRM.summary: A short clip of Stephen Fry defending swearing as a rich and essential part of the English language and rejecting the idea that it is unnecessary.
s_osQvkeNRM.why: HN commenters post it in swearing and profanity debates as the best statement against taking offense at profanity.

snz7JJlSZvw.summary: A roughly 90-minute film of John Dobson building a Dobsonian telescope step by step, including hand-grinding the mirror.
snz7JJlSZvw.why: Recommended to anyone interested in telescope making as a guide from Dobson himself.

suRDUFpsHus.summary: The Kodak Carousel pitch scene from the Mad Men season finale, in which Don Draper sells nostalgia through a slide projector. It runs about three minutes.
suRDUFpsHus.why: HN holds it up as one of the best pitches ever, an example of selling feeling and nostalgia rather than features.

s254IPHXgVA.summary: Jean-Marc Jancovici gives an MIT Media Lab talk on whether technology can save us from climate change. He argues from a physical view of energy that economic growth, energy use and climate impact are tightly linked.
s254IPHXgVA.why: Recommended in climate and energy threads as a numbers-based explanation of why energy underlies growth and emissions.

s8nFqwOho-s.summary: Johann Korndorfer's NVScene 2015 talk on building content with signed distance functions. It focuses on patterns that make SDF modelling more structured, arguing that SDFs capture a shape's essence like vector graphics do compared with polygons or voxels.
s8nFqwOho-s.why: Recommended as an excellent talk from a demoscene practitioner on how to build sophisticated scenes from distance functions.

sBzRwzY7G-k.summary: LearnCode.academy presents a roadmap of web development technologies to learn in 2016 and 2017, spanning front-end, back-end and DevOps tools.
sBzRwzY7G-k.why: Recommended to beginners asking how to start in web development as a compact survey of the toolscape of its time.

sI5Ftm1-jik.summary: ElectroBOOM's Mehdi Sadaghdar explains how a full bridge rectifier works, the building block of AC to DC converters, with his usual humor and a demonstration of the circuit.
sI5Ftm1-jik.why: Recommended as an enlightening and funny explanation of bridge rectifiers, often linked in power supply teardown threads.

sPFmKu2S5XY.summary: Dr. Russell Barkley lectures on the neuroanatomy of ADHD and how to treat it, linking executive function and working memory to the disorder. It is part 3 of a CADDAC series.
sPFmKu2S5XY.why: HN commenters recommend it to people with ADHD for helping them understand their behavior and how their brain works.

sSfejgwbDQ8.summary: Jon Stewart appears on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and discusses the pandemic, vaccine science and the Wuhan lab origin theory. He jokes that the disease shares its name with the lab.
sSfejgwbDQ8.why: HN posts it in COVID origin threads as a blunt comedic take on why the lab leak question deserved investigation rather than dismissal.

sfGtw2C95Ms.summary: Clayton Christensen explains the jobs-to-be-done idea in five minutes, using the fast-food milkshake example. The point is that understanding the job a product is hired to do makes it easier to improve.
sfGtw2C95Ms.why: Cited as the short, famous introduction to Jobs To Be Done and competition framing.

sfXn_ecH5Rw.summary: Adam Neely interviews Damien Riehl and Noah Rubin about their project to generate and copyright every possible melody as MIDI. The video explains their reasoning and how it bears on music copyright lawsuits.
sfXn_ecH5Rw.why: It is the go-to explainer whenever HN discusses brute-forcing melodies, copyright, or AI-generated content, since it features the project's creators.

st571DYYTR8.summary: James Hoffmann demonstrates his technique for a clean, sludge-free cup from a French press: stir, break the crust, wait, and carefully pour. It is a four-minute guide.
st571DYYTR8.why: HN commenters swear by it as the best way to make French press coffee, and cite its 16:1 water-to-coffee ratio.

s0ukXDnWlTY.summary: Geekerwan reviews smartphone CPUs by power efficiency rather than benchmark scores, with test methodology and chapters on Qualcomm, Apple, Samsung and Google chips. It explains why high benchmark scores can coexist with heat and poor battery life.
s0ukXDnWlTY.why: HN people cite it as detailed data on mobile SoC efficiency, sustained performance and ARM core efficiency curves.

s9aCwCKgkLo.summary: People Make Games interviewed 16 current and former Valve employees to examine how the company's no-bosses, no-titles structure works in practice, and where it falls short.
s9aCwCKgkLo.why: Recommended as well-researched, interview-based coverage of the Valve model and its failures, often linked in threads about Valve and flat organizations.

s9fByRmAHgU.summary: Part 2 of a Q&A workshop with security researcher Jacob Appelbaum from April 2012, covering mobile phone security, cellphone forensics, state repression and surveillance. Topics include booting Tails from USB and surveillance self-defense resources.
s9fByRmAHgU.why: Recommended as a practical talk on privacy and anonymity options, including diskless laptops running Tails.

sCZJblyT_XM.summary: Gary Bernhardt's Cascadia Ruby Conference 2011 talk on using the Unix shell for practical problem solving. He builds pipelines interactively by iterative refinement, using small tools as levers.
sCZJblyT_XM.why: Recommended as a brilliant demonstration of how to think in Unix pipelines.

sI1C9DyIi_8.summary: Physicist Albert Bartlett's full-length lecture on how steady exponential growth in population and energy use collides with finite resources. It uses examples like bacteria in a bottle and covers peak oil.
sI1C9DyIi_8.why: HN repeatedly quotes its thesis that humanity's greatest shortcoming is failing to understand the exponential function.

sKudSeqHSJk.summary: About Here looks at the housing crisis and argues for non-market solutions such as co-op and social housing, drawing on Vancouver's situation. It discusses how public supply can hold down rents.
sKudSeqHSJk.why: Recommended in housing threads as a decent dive into the problem and possible long-term solutions.

sbQhgEJuExY.summary: Masagin is a realtime demoscene production by Farbrausch and Neuro with music by paniq, using animated recursive SVG graphics made in Inkscape. It is a psychedelic, nested-dials audiovisual piece.
sbQhgEJuExY.why: HN recommends it as a showcase of what the demoscene can do, with high-res antialiased vector graphics and motion blur.

sg2j7mZ9-2Y.summary: jan Misali traces the history of the letter W, including why it is called double u. The video is part of a series of deep dives into individual letters.
sg2j7mZ9-2Y.why: Recommended for readers who enjoy fascinating deep dives into the history of odd letters and the alphabet.

sycgL3Qg_Ak.summary: A five-minute CBC Radio WireTap farewell video in which people of all ages offer words of wisdom to younger people. The advice is short and funny, and keeps coming back to the point that nobody really knows what they are doing.
sycgL3Qg_Ak.why: Commenters bring it up in threads about life advice and aging as the best advice they have heard, namely to ignore advice and do your own thing.

szIGZVrSAyc.summary: Yanis Varoufakis and Noam Chomsky talk on stage at the New York Public Library in 2016. They cover the Greek financial crisis, European politics, neoliberalism and America's economic future, drawing on Varoufakis's book.
szIGZVrSAyc.why: Recommended as a long, insightful conversation that gives a view of how Greece was pressured during the bailouts.

s10etP1p2bU.summary: Jacques Pepin makes a classic French omelette in a short uncut demonstration. The video contrasts it with the American style.
s10etP1p2bU.why: HN people recommend it as a simple method that makes omelettes approachable, while noting that the technique is harder than it looks.

sJj9y4t9UnU.summary: The main theme from Eduard Artemyev's score to the 1979 Soviet film Siberiade, an electronic piece that features the ANS synthesizer.
sJj9y4t9UnU.why: Shared as an example of Artemyev, called the Russian Vangelis, and of great Soviet electronic film music.

sKOk4Y4inVY.summary: Eben Moglen's re:publica 2012 talk argues that media which spy on and data-mine the public threaten freedom of thought, and that free technology and free culture are needed to protect it.
sKOk4Y4inVY.why: HN users recommend Moglen as a brilliant speaker and a top introduction to free software philosophy, and cite this talk in privacy and crypto-wars discussions.

sNhhvQGsMEc.summary: Kurzgesagt introduces the Fermi paradox: with so many stars and planets, why do we see no sign of aliens? It sets up the question and what it might imply for our own future. It is part 1 of 2.
sNhhvQGsMEc.why: HN commenters recommend the two-part Kurzgesagt pair as an engaging, accessible introduction to the Fermi paradox and the Great Filter.

sTu3LwpF6XI.summary: Ben Eater shows how to build logic gates out of transistors, including NOR gates. It is part of his clear hardware-from-scratch teaching style.
sTu3LwpF6XI.why: HN people recommend Ben Eater's videos for easy, clear explanations of digital logic and building computers.

sfrYOWlKJ_g.summary: Louis Rossmann, an independent Apple repair shop owner, explains why he does not use Apple products, drawing on his experience of repairing devices he considers designed to fail and hard to fix.
sfrYOWlKJ_g.why: Cited in right-to-repair and Apple threads as an insider's view of Apple hardware design and repairability.

sgHbC6udIqc.summary: Ned Batchelder's PyCon 2012 talk gives a quick overview of what Unicode is, then focuses on what a Python programmer needs to handle text correctly. It presents the 'Unicode sandwich' strategy: decode bytes at input, work with Unicode internally, encode at output.
sgHbC6udIqc.why: Commenters point to it as the clearest explanation of Python's bytes versus Unicode model and the Unicode sandwich, which finally makes the confusion click.

s19G6n0UjsM.summary: A guest lecture Jon Gjengset gave at Two Sigma on using Rust for large, high-performance systems. It covers why Rust suits such projects, the Noria research database, a concurrent data structure used in it, and practical experience.
s19G6n0UjsM.why: HN points to it as a detailed, captivating talk by the Noria author, including a good explanation of deduplicating data between maps using unsafe.

s2xrarUWVRQ.summary: JerryRigEverything tours Li-Cycle to show how lithium-ion batteries from EVs, phones and tools are recycled. It walks through the process of shredding batteries and extracting materials.
s2xrarUWVRQ.why: HN points to it as evidence that battery recycling is more advanced and practical than people assume.

sFrVdoOhu1Q.summary: Dan Gelbart shows his home-built air bearing CNC lathe and grinder, which reaches about 1 micron accuracy. He demonstrates the machine and its parts.
sFrVdoOhu1Q.why: Cited as a marvel of absurd precision in home-built machine tools, and a pointer to Gelbart's other videos.

sIi_QS1tdFM.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on sponsored content in local news. John Oliver explains why local news integrity matters and how paid content disguised as news erodes it.
sIi_QS1tdFM.why: HN links it in threads about native advertising and disguised ads as a good, funny overview of sponsored content passing as news.

sJFnWZH5FXc.summary: Retro Game Mechanics Explained shows how the Atari 2600 draws images with almost no video memory, by having the CPU race the CRT beam line by line. It walks through the techniques in detail.
sJFnWZH5FXc.why: Cited as the go-to demonstration of how hard and clever Atari 2600 graphics programming was.

saRir95iIWk.summary: A 1984 AT&T film showing the live cutover of a Glendale, California central office from step-by-step switching to an electronic switching system. Installers prepare the site and then cut cables in a coordinated operation.
saRir95iIWk.why: HN links it as a vivid example of high-stakes telco cutovers, done with careful coordination, big cable cutters and under a minute of downtime.

sf5OrthVRPA.summary: Matt Parker's LMS popular lecture on how seemingly incredible results can be meaningless random patterns. He ranges from ancient Woolworths civilisations to shoelaces and DNA.
sf5OrthVRPA.why: Used to illustrate that humans pattern-match and find spurious patterns in enough data points.

si9iqF5uTFk.summary: Part one of Capt. Grace Hopper's 1982 NSA lecture on the future of data, hardware, software and people. It includes her humor, her nanosecond demonstration and views on scaling and resisting old ways of doing things.
si9iqF5uTFk.why: HN enjoys it as a funny, quotable lecture from a bygone era, with lines about horizontal scaling and change that still resonate.

ssZ_8cqfBlE.summary: Tom Scott tours Ocado's automated grocery warehouse, where thousands of robots move boxes on a grid called the Hive, and asks whether they are individual robots or a hive mind.
ssZ_8cqfBlE.why: Cited in automation and robotics threads as the example of a warehouse built robot-first.

ssob-7sGVWs.summary: Cathode Ray Dude covers two bizarre HP 'Quick Start' features: QuickLook, an offline email client built on EFI firmware, and Daystarter, which hijacks the Windows boot process. It includes an explanation of EFI applications and why HP built these things.
ssob-7sGVWs.why: Cited as a deep, entertaining look at firmware-level software and vendors abusing pre-boot access.

suo_aUTUpps.summary: A short explainer from Nat and Friends on where Google Earth's 3D imagery comes from, how it is stitched together, and how often it is updated. It describes aircraft carrying camera rigs and photogrammetry that turns the photos into 3D models.
suo_aUTUpps.why: People link it as the quick answer to how Google builds 3D maps, and as evidence that planes are still used to capture the imagery.

swQbA4zub20.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2018 talk on how AWS limits the blast radius of failures. It covers design techniques such as cell-based architecture and shuffle sharding.
swQbA4zub20.why: It is the go-to reference whenever HN discusses cell-based architecture and outage isolation, as an explanation straight from AWS engineers.

syoqjYLDs48.summary: A Startup School 2013 session where Paul Graham and Sam Altman hold live office hours with startups including CodeCombat, Flexport and others. The founders pitch and get on-the-spot feedback.
syoqjYLDs48.why: HN points to it as a look at what YC office hours are like and as an early glimpse of Flexport and CodeCombat pitching.

sAz_UvnUeuU.summary: A Burnistoun sketch from BBC Scotland in which two men try to use a voice-recognition elevator that cannot understand their Scottish accents.
sAz_UvnUeuU.why: Posted as the obligatory joke in any thread about speech recognition, and recommended in a thread on what makes people laugh.

shFUDPqVmTg.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder reads a confidential email and uses it to explain her worries about academia and incentives in theoretical physics research. She ties it to her earlier Nature Physics comment on research quality.
shFUDPqVmTg.why: Cited in threads about science funding and trust in research as an angry insider critique of academic incentives, though some commenters doubt it.

s-CTkbHnpNQ.summary: A one-minute clip from Tom Sachs's Ten Bullets series on the rule "Always Be Knolling", which means constantly arranging and putting away unused objects.
s-CTkbHnpNQ.why: Used as a short intro to knolling and as an analogy for tidying workspaces and continuously cleaning up code.

s4QOHe4bOZc.summary: A one-minute demo comparing RetroArch shaders on the Sonic the Hedgehog waterfall, where Sega Genesis dithering creates a transparency effect. It shows how different shaders emulate the CRT look.
s4QOHe4bOZc.why: HN cites it as the example showing why CRT emulation is needed to render effects the original artists intended.

s65BigoMV_I.summary: Chris Lattner and Brennan Saeta present Swift for TensorFlow at the TensorFlow Dev Summit 2019, covering language-integrated automatic differentiation and tooling for machine learning in Swift.
s65BigoMV_I.why: Cited as the source for Google's Swift for TensorFlow effort, later remembered as a once-hyped ML language.

sB4RYBpwV0A.summary: The opening track of Charanjit Singh's 1982 album Synthesizing: Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat, recorded in Bombay. It plays Indian raga forms on a Roland Jupiter-8, TB-303 and TR-808 over a disco beat.
sB4RYBpwV0A.why: HN points to it as an early acid-style record that came before Chicago acid house, and as a way into ragas for electronic music fans.

sCr_gb8rdEI.summary: GitHub interviews Linus Torvalds on twenty years of Git, from its creation in about ten days as a Linux kernel tool to its role in modern software development. He discusses technical decisions, community contributions and the project's philosophy.
sCr_gb8rdEI.why: HN commenters cite it for Linus's direct opinions on Git and development tooling, such as calling the SHA-256 migration pointless churn.

sI-1YNAmWlk.summary: Not Just Bikes visits Paris to see how Mayor Anne Hidalgo's policies are turning it into a '100% cyclable' city. It looks at the changes that took space from cars for bikes and people.
sI-1YNAmWlk.why: Referenced in urban planning threads on making cities less car-centric, and the channel is recommended for road and bike safety.

sJtm0MoOgiU.summary: Lawyer and musician Damien Riehl argues that music is math with a finite number of melodies, and describes how he and programmer Noah Rubin generated every possible melody and released them under CC0 to avoid accidental infringement claims.
sJtm0MoOgiU.why: HN cites it as the stunt behind 'copyright every melody' in threads about music copyright, takedowns and AI authorship.

sLCHg9mUBag.summary: The 1966 film Walt Disney recorded weeks before his death, laying out his plans for the Florida Project and especially EPCOT, a planned city of the future. It uses models, concept art and animation to describe the circular city, monorails and people movers.
sLCHg9mUBag.why: HN cites it in discussions of planned cities and urban design as the original source for Disney's utopian EPCOT vision.

sLFaa6RPJIU.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science shows how to make and test YBCO high-temperature superconductor with a kiln and eBay chemicals. He demonstrates flux pinning and shows a close-up of the crystal structure.
sLFaa6RPJIU.why: HN points to it in superconductor and LK-99 threads as evidence that YBCO can be made in a modest home lab.

sQ56ve39l2I.summary: JerryRigEverything puts the iPhone Air through scratch, bend and durability tests and is surprised that the ultra-thin phone proves very tough. The video is sponsored by dbrand cases.
sQ56ve39l2I.why: Cited as evidence against the assumption that thin modern phones are fragile.

sR8M4zARBXY.summary: The Thought Emporium synthesizes chicken noodle soup from pure chemicals, following an original patent for artificial chicken flavor. The video explores how many chemicals it takes to make a convincing soup.
sR8M4zARBXY.why: Brought up in threads on synthetic food and flavor as a fun example of building a dish from chemicals.

sWFFiubtC3c.summary: A SpaceX concept animation showing the planned fully reusable Falcon 9, with both first and second stages performing vertical landings.
sWFFiubtC3c.why: Linked as a historical artifact of SpaceX's early reusability ambitions, including the once-planned reusable second stage.

sWN13pKVp9s.summary: Lieutenant General Mark Hertling gives a TEDx talk arguing that obesity and poor youth fitness are a national security problem because too few young Americans can meet military physical requirements.
sWN13pKVp9s.why: HN cites it in threads on military recruiting and obesity as an early warning from a senior general that still applies.

sXPOw2unxy0.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything segment arguing that political motives, including Nixon's, lay behind making marijuana illegal. It mixes comedy with history.
sXPOw2unxy0.why: Cited in cannabis and drug-war threads as an eye-opening look at the political reasons for criminalization.

sXwDrcd1t-E.summary: The creator of ESPARGOS, an ESP32-based antenna array from the University of Stuttgart, explains how it senses phase and amplitude of WiFi signals to localize devices and build a WiFi camera. It demos the Python library and project.
sXwDrcd1t-E.why: Recommended as the companion explanation to the Espargos project, showing how phase and time differences localize devices.

sln-gJaURzk.summary: A fireside Q&A with the Go team (Pike, Thompson, Griesemer and others) at Google I/O 2012. They answer audience questions about Go's design, goals, garbage collection plans and future.
sln-gJaURzk.why: HN people cite it for candid answers straight from Go's creators, including Ken Thompson on how the complexity of C++0x motivated Go.

sqIz-RNUL1g.summary: A DEFCON 20 panel with NSA whistleblower William Binney, journalist James Bamford and ACLU lawyers on the NSA's mass collection of communications and its conflict with the Constitution.
sqIz-RNUL1g.why: HN points to it as a prescient talk that discussed, in 2012, much of what Snowden's leaks later confirmed.

sumZLwFXJqE.summary: An Extra Credits episode on how MMO economies get overrun by inflation when players can mint unlimited gold by killing monsters. It covers approaches borrowed from real-world economics, such as anchoring or pegging currency, as alternatives to simple gold sinks.
sumZLwFXJqE.why: Cited in game-economy threads as a clear explanation of why vendor-sellable loot causes hyperinflation and how designers counter it.

svEuG_ekNT0.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on US voting machines, covering how they work, their security weaknesses, and how elections could be made more secure.
svEuG_ekNT0.why: Cited in election security threads as a watchable overview of voting machine problems.

s-mOy8VUEBk.summary: A sketch from the Norwegian NRK show Uti Var Hage poking fun at the Danish language and how hard it is to understand.
s-mOy8VUEBk.why: HN posts it as a joke in threads about Denmark, Danes or languages that are hard to understand.

s93KC4AGKnY.summary: The final scene of the 1983 film WarGames, in which the WOPR computer runs through nuclear war scenarios and concludes that the only winning move is not to play. It is a six-minute clip uploaded in higher quality than earlier copies.
s93KC4AGKnY.why: HN cites it as shorthand for the tic-tac-toe lesson, especially in threads about AI and nuclear strategy or games that cannot be won.

sFBOQzSk14c.summary: A clip from Monty Python's Life of Brian in which Stan says he wants to be a woman and have babies.
sFBOQzSk14c.why: HN uses it as a joke or as an early example of satire about gender identity in threads on those topics.

sGArqoF0TpQ.summary: An SMBC Theater sketch in which JP Nickel presents 'both sides' on every issue, satirizing false balance in news coverage.
sGArqoF0TpQ.why: Brought up as a joke when threads touch on false balance, media platforming or both-sides debates.

sHzdsFiBbFc.summary: A short spoof of a nature documentary shows spiders building webs after being given various drugs. It is an early internet comedy classic.
